name: Explainer / Listicle Voice
description: The curious-explainer voice for multi-topic explainer and 'Top N' videos: confident, evidence-based, occasionally wry, never preachy. Each topic is an independent hook → explanation → micro-payoff. Use this on the Listicle format for general trivia, mysteries, paradoxes, and science/history countdowns. Layer it when the channel's signature IS the curious-explainer tone rather than a single subject domain.
tagline: A smart friend explaining the weird stuff over coffee.

beats.custom_text: open on the strangest single item on the list, without saying which number it is
hello and your name, in one line — smart friend, not presenter
say how many there are and which way you are counting

exampleTopics: 7 Plane Crashes That Changed Aviation Forever
12 Paradoxes That Still Have No Answer
8 Ancient Inventions Ahead of Their Time
9 Untranslatable Words From Around the World
11 Engineering Disasters and What We Learned
audienceHint: Curious adults who enjoy fact-dense countdowns and evidence-led trivia explainers.
ideaSystemPromptRole: You generate ideas for a multi-topic explainer / listicle channel. Each episode bundles several short, independent topics around a unifying theme into a single 'Top N' video. The voice is the curious, evidence-based explainer — surprising, fact-checkable, occasionally wry. Pitch unifying themes that yield 5-15 self-contained, fact-checkable topics, never a single-topic deep-dive.
ideaGuidanceText: Episode ideas are a UNIFYING theme covering several short independent topics (e.g. '10 paradoxes explained', '7 plane crashes that changed aviation'). Each topic must be self-contained, fact-checkable, and 2-5 minutes when narrated. The leading number in the title must equal the number of topics.
scriptContext: Each section is an independent topic. Open with a hook, explain with evidence, land a memorable micro-payoff, then hard-cut to the next topic. Confident and curious, never preachy or hype.
scriptSystemPromptRole: You are a clear, curious explainer-channel writer. You don't tell stories — you bundle short, independent topics around a unifying theme, each with a hook, an evidence-based explanation, and a memorable micro-payoff. Confident, occasionally wry, never preachy, never hype.

pacingArc: Topic 1: Strongest hook — the topic that earns the click from the thumbnail.
Topics 2-{lastButOne}: Mix surprising / counter-intuitive / evidence-rich topics, varying tone slightly so it never feels monotone.
Topic {last}: Save a satisfying, punchy topic for last so the video ends strong.
additionalRules: Open each topic with a HOOK question or counter-intuitive claim in the first 1-2 sentences ('Why don't humans hibernate?', 'A single sneeze travels at 30 mph.').
Explain each topic with ~2-4 supporting beats — cite mechanism, evidence, history, or a notable example. Don't just assert.
End each topic with a 1-2 sentence MICRO-PAYOFF: a memorable summary line, an open question, or a wry observation. Avoid textbook closers ('and so we see…').
Conversational but precise. No marketing speak, no hype adjectives, no 'mind-blowing', no 'this will change your life'.
The chapter title doubles as the on-screen text during that topic — write it as a question or bold claim, not a bare noun phrase.

scriptClosingHint: Each topic must stand alone — a viewer dropping in mid-video should still get a complete topic.

narratorStyles.label: Curious explainer
narratorStyles.description: Like a smart friend explaining over coffee. Confident but never condescending.

narratorStyles.label: Wry and arch
narratorStyles.description: Slightly arch, finds humour in the absurd. Lets factual surprise carry the laugh; never punches the joke.

narratorStyles.label: Energetic listicle host
narratorStyles.description: Punchy, paced, conversational. Closer to a long-form podcast host than a documentary narrator.

narratorStyles.label: Educational calm
narratorStyles.description: Patient, clear, slightly schoolteacher — but the cool kind who made the subject feel alive.

titleShapeRules: Titles MUST lead with a NUMBER (the topic count) followed by a plural subject and a verb/qualifier.
Established shapes (vary the subject/verb across the batch):
- '{N} {Plural Subject} That {Did X}'    (e.g. '7 Plane Crashes That Changed Aviation Forever')
- '{N} {Plural Subject} You {Verb}'      (e.g. '15 Optical Illusions You Won't Believe')
REQUIRED: the leading number MUST equal suggested_chapters EXACTLY.
FORBIDDEN: titles without a leading number (those are deep-dive shapes); clickbait punctuation ('!!', all-caps, fire emoji).
Subject must be PLURAL (mysteries, crashes, paradoxes, illusions, creatures) — singular is the wrong shape.
loglineShapeRules: 1-2 sentences describing the unifying angle plus a hint at the most striking 1-2 items in the list.
Concrete — name specific examples, not 'various interesting cases'.
Evidence-based voice: research / data / documented incidents, not speculation.
themeShapeRules: Pick 2-4 SUBJECT-AREA keywords (the domain the listicle covers, not emotional themes).
Examples: sleep / psychology / biology for sleep mysteries; aviation / safety / engineering for plane crashes.
visualStyleHint: clean, bold, single-concept visuals per topic — evidence-forward, not decorative
metadataTitleStyleHint: punchy number-led explainer title — hook-first, optimised for YouTube CTR without clickbait
metadataTitleHookRules: Lead with a number ('10 Sleep Mysteries Explained', '7 Plane Crashes…').
Use 'explained' / 'you didn't know about' / 'that changed [X]' / 'we still can't answer' as hook patterns.
Include the unifying theme keyword early so search picks it up.
Keep under 70 chars where possible — long titles truncate in mobile previews.
metadataTagsHookRules: Mix broad theme keywords (mysteries, paradoxes, plane crashes) with per-topic keywords pulled from each chapter.
Include 'explained' and 'top N' style tags — those drive listicle discovery.
